gallery.title: File:Skoteini-Alea-Polje Peloponnese Greece.jpg
gallery.description:
View on part of the plateau  Skotiní-Aléa, Argolis (a valleylike 14 km long karst depression, 560 m, polje), on all sides surrounded by mountains. There are two extensions off the valley, where the two villages Skotiní and Aléa rest on steep slopes. Relatively frequent geological phenomenon in the karst basins of the northeast Peloponnese, Greece.
The valley plateau has no natural surface water outlet. Precipitation must be drained by ditches. When precipitation of winters is exceptionally rich, some agricultural fields may become wet. Depending on the capacity of the ditches and the two geologically old ponors, some fields may even be flooded. The southern section of the plateau has an up to 30 m extra deep and 2 km long depression, in which precipitation creates a temporary lake, for which the ponor must turn active. See the Foto: Image:Alea Argolidas.JPG.

gallery.title: File:Polje-Orchomenus Arcadia Peloponnese.jpg
gallery.description:
Plateau Orchomenus (a karst depression in 625 m. polje), on all sides surrounded by mountains. On its borders are the villages Levidi, Vlacherna, Hotoussa, Limni, Kandila, Arcadia. Relatively frequent geological phenomenon in the karst basins of the northeast Peloponnese, Greece.
The basin has no natural surface water outlet. Precipitation must be drained by ditches, the two ponors and an artifical tunnel. When precipitation of winters is exceptionally rich, some agricultural fields may be wet or even flooded. Depending on the capacity of the ditches and the geologically old ponors, a temporary lake may result even nowadays. The ancient author Pausanias reports of the existence of the lake, see Orchomenus.  Looking south, in the far back: Village Vlacherna.

gallery.title: File:Argon-Field Nestani-Polje Arcadi Peloponnese.jpg
gallery.description:
Beautiful pasture of a plateau, with the village Nestani high above. The plateau is well drained by old wells and ditches (a karst basin/depression, 630 m). Relatively frequent geological phenomenon in the karst basins of the northeast Peloponnese, Greece.
The plateau has no natural surface water outlet. When precipitation of winters is exceptionally rich, the soil is wet. In spite of keeping the ditches and the ponor clean, the quantity of water may create a temporary lake even nowadays.

gallery.description: Typical housing with some agriculture in the plateau of Mantineia, a section of the very large  Plateau (a karst basin/depression, in 670 m). Relatively frequent geological phenomenon in the karst basins of the northeast Peloponnese, Greece.

gallery.title: File:Kandila-Valley Peloponnese Greece.jpg
gallery.description:
Kandila section of the Plateau Orchomenus, a karst basin/depression in 630 m, (polje). Kandila Plateau is the north eastern extension of the large basin, with the village Kandia on its slope. Relatively frequent geological phenomenon in the karst basins of the northeast Peloponnese, Greece.
The plateau has no natural surface water outlet. Precipitation must be drained by ditches. When precipitation of winters is exceptionally rich, some agricultural fields may be wet or even flooded. Depending on the capacity of the ditches and the geologically old ponors at the Plateau Orchomenus’ western section, a temporary lake may result even nowadays.

gallery.title: File:Karst-spring Achaea Greece.jpg
gallery.description:
karst spring in district Achaea, Peloponnese, Greece in May 2006. The ca. 20m wide oval spring pit, shaded by big trees, discharges seasonally varying, but enormous quantities of water, as may be seen on the photo, made from right behind the spring. There is a large catchment area: The snow covered massif Aroania and the katavothren (Greek term for ponors) of the depression plateau Feneos. The fast transport through large joints of tectonic origin indicates a lack of long aquifer-filtering.
Unfortunately this jewel of a spring is not (nature-)protected, but untouched in its hidden seclusion!

gallery.title: File:Planitero Aroanios-Springs Achaea Peloponnese.jpg
gallery.description:
karst springs, Achaea, Peloponnese. The springs emerge partly from hard and partly from loose sediment, a ground of sandy gravel, well shaded by broad-leaved trees. The water comes from the carbonate Aroania Mountains (1500- 2341 m) and also from joints fed by the katavothren (Greek term for ponors/sinkholes) of the Feneos depression. On a surface of only 30x800 m many tiny outflows result in a remarkable large brook: River Aroanios.
Unfortunately this rare kind of a geotope is not protected at all! No directives, no administrative surveillance! The place is dominated by tourist-commercial interests.

gallery.title: File:Sintzi-Spring Upper-Arcadia Karst-basin Peloponnese Greece.jpg
gallery.description:
en:Karst spring „Sintzi“, located in the large karst basin Vlacherna/Hotoussa/Kandila in Arcadia (Peloponnese). The karst water rises up from a cave, 186m deep (2015).
The amount of the water varies, according to rainfall and season. While the mountain is basically limestone, the flat is highly accumulated, loamy soil and below, remains of scree.
